lab_title: Human Heart Anatomy and Blood Flow Pathway
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers, four valves, and major vessels of the human heart.
Trace deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through pulmonary and systemic circulation in correct sequence.
Explain how valves prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle.
Relate ventricular wall thickness to the different pumping demands of pulmonary versus systemic circulation.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the heart as a three-dimensional organ and establish anterior/posterior, superior/inferior, and right/left orientation before internal anatomy is examined.
key_visuals: Life-sized rotating heart model with anterior surface facing the student
Color cues distinguishing right heart/deoxygenated side and left heart/oxygenated side
Visible apex, base, coronary sulcus, and major vessel openings
student_actions: Rotate and scale the heart model to inspect it from multiple angles.
Use orientation prompts to identify the apex, base, anatomical right, and anatomical left.
Confirm that anatomical right appears on the viewer’s left when facing the anterior heart.

scenes.brief_purpose: Reveal the internal chambers and compare the structural differences between atria and ventricles, especially left versus right ventricular myocardium.
key_visuals: Cutaway heart showing right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle
Labels appearing as students select each chamber
Cross-section highlighting thin atrial walls and thicker ventricular walls
Side-by-side emphasis on left ventricle versus right ventricle wall thickness
student_actions: Tap each chamber in response to identification prompts.
Compare atrial and ventricular wall thickness using the cutaway view.
Explain why the left ventricle has the thickest myocardium.

scenes.scene_name: 3. Mapping Major Vessels Entering and Leaving the Heart
scenes.brief_purpose: Connect each major vessel to the chamber it enters or exits and distinguish pulmonary from systemic pathways.
key_visuals: Heart model with superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, and aorta emphasized
Directional arrows at vessel openings
Blue pathway cues for deoxygenated blood and red cues for oxygenated blood
student_actions: Match vessel labels to the correct anatomical structures.
Trace which vessels bring blood into the heart and which carry blood away.
Classify each vessel as part of pulmonary or systemic circulation.

scenes.scene_name: 4. Following Deoxygenated Blood Through the Right Heart
scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the first half of the circulation pathway from systemic venous return through the right heart to the lungs.
key_visuals: Animated blue blood particles entering through the superior and inferior vena cava
Right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, and pulmonary arteries highlighted in sequence
Simplified lung icons receiving blood from pulmonary arteries
student_actions: Advance the animation step-by-step from venae cavae to pulmonary arteries.
Select each structure as the blood reaches it.
Arrange pathway cards in order for deoxygenated blood flow.

scenes.scene_name: 5. Following Oxygenated Blood Through the Left Heart
scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the second half of circulation from pulmonary venous return through the left heart to systemic outflow.
key_visuals: Animated red blood particles returning from lung icons through pulmonary veins
Left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and aorta highlighted in sequence
Systemic body outline receiving blood from the aorta
student_actions: Advance the animation from pulmonary veins to aorta.
Identify the two left-side valves as blood passes through them.
Arrange pathway cards in order for oxygenated blood flow.

scenes.scene_name: 6. Valves and One-Way Flow During the Cardiac Cycle
scenes.brief_purpose: Show how atrioventricular and semilunar valves open and close to prevent backflow during filling and ejection.
key_visuals: Close-up transparent heart with tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves visible
Valve leaflets opening and closing during simplified diastole and systole
Backflow attempt animation blocked by closed valve leaflets
student_actions: Trigger diastole and systole animations and observe which valves open or close.
Predict whether each valve should be open or closed at key moments.
Explain how valve closure preserves one-way flow.

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate the full pathway by having students assemble and narrate the complete pulmonary and systemic circuit.
key_visuals: Full heart-lung-body circulation diagram surrounding the 3D heart
Continuous blue-to-red-to-systemic flow animation
Checkpoint labels for chambers, valves, and vessels
student_actions: Trace the complete blood flow pathway from body to heart to lungs to heart to body.
Place missing labels on chambers, valves, and vessels.
Complete a final sequence check that links structure, flow direction, oxygenation status, and pumping demand.
